summary: Iter 154 — Project Request Center (unified 9-type workflow). Backend: 24/24 pytest passed (/app/backend/tests/test_iter154_project_requests.py). All required flows validated end-to-end: 9 types with dept/stockable/payment flags; stock-check with Pen and Paper in-stock + unknown-item shortfall (any_short/all_in_stock correct); PM creates material (1-step chain, dept=stores), vehicle_manpower 8000x6=48000 large-value (3-step chain dept_head→GM→Director, dept=logistics), fuel 5000 (dept=admin, 1-step); sales role → 403; wrong-role approve → 403; Project Head approves small material → with_dept and stores notification created (fallback super_admin); large-value vehicle needs 3 approvals; reject sets status=rejected; raise-pr converts shortfall to purchase_requisitions (source='project_request') and sets pr_raised/pr_number; raise-pr on no-shortfall → 400; raise-pr on non-stockable → 400; fulfil on material/stores flips to fulfilled; fulfil on fuel (payment) auto-creates project_expenses row with source='project_request', status='approved_for_payment', AND accounts@erp.com receives 'Request For Payment' notification; wrong-dept role fulfil → 403; close after fulfilled → closed; DELETE on non-pending/rejected → 400; filters (project_code, request_type, status, dept) and summary counters work; xlsx and pdf exports return >100 bytes with correct content-type. ui_bugs.issue: Stock Check button triggers 422 pydantic float_parsing on empty-string monthly_rate/months (and amount) because runStockCheck() posts the raw form as-is (fields default to ''), while create() normalises to Number|null. Reproduced: 422 detail says 'Input should be a valid number, unable to parse string as a number' for body.monthly_rate and body.months. User sees toast 'Stock check failed' and req-stock-result never appears.

React console warning 'Encountered two children with the same key' printed repeatedly on this page (~30 occurrences during load). Non-fatal but indicates duplicate keys — likely in a shared component (menu/nav or table). Investigate.

integration_issues.issue: Blank monthly_rate/months/amount posted as empty strings → backend 422; user cannot preview stock unless they've picked a request_type that never populates those fields. Fix: coerce '' → null in runStockCheck payload (same normalisation as create()).

action_items: FIX (frontend, HIGH): In /app/frontend/src/pages/ops/ProjectRequests.jsx runStockCheck(), normalise the payload the same way create() does — coerce empty strings for monthly_rate, months, amount to null (or omit them). Otherwise backend Pydantic RequestIn rejects with 422 on Check Stock for any request_type whose form initialised these as ''. Example: const payload = { ...form, amount: form.amount?Number(form.amount):null, monthly_rate: form.monthly_rate?Number(form.monthly_rate):null, months: form.months?Number(form.months):null, items: form.items };
OPTIONAL (backend): Loosen RequestIn to accept '' as None for Optional[float] fields via a validator so the API is forgiving to any client. Alternative to (1).
critical_code_review_comments: project_requests_router.close_request has no status guard — allows closing a request in any status (even pending_approval/rejected). Consider restricting to status in ('fulfilled','with_dept','pr_raised').

project_requests_router.py raise_pr allows status 'pending_approval' as well as 'with_dept' — the docstring/spec says PR is raised after Project Head approves. Allowing it pre-approval could leak un-approved shortfalls into procurement. Suggest restricting to 'with_dept' only.
_notify_dept and _book_expense both silently swallow all exceptions (bare except Exception: pass). Wrap with logging so failures are visible in supervisor logs, not silently missed.

Frontend: STOCKABLE set is duplicated on client (line 19) — kept in sync manually with backend REQUEST_TYPES. Consider deriving from GET /project-requests/types response (meta.stockable) to prevent drift.

Detail dialog approve/reject visibility guard has an operator-precedence bug: (user?.role === (detail.chain||[])[current_step]?.role || user?.role === 'super_admin') — the outer '&&' with '(A || B)' works only because the surrounding parentheses are present. It reads correctly but is fragile; add data-testid-based unit test.
Router path GET /project-requests/export.{fmt} uses a path param — works but bypasses OpenAPI enum; consider ?format=xlsx query.
No test for user without project_requests permission — implicit via require_permission but not covered explicitly for read on a non-listed role.

rca of the issue: Frontend runStockCheck() line 77 posts `{ ...form, items: form.items }` where form is initialised via blank() containing monthly_rate:'', months:'', amount:''. The backend endpoint uses the same RequestIn Pydantic model (Optional[float]) which does NOT coerce empty string to None (Pydantic v2 behaviour). Result: HTTP 422 with float_parsing errors for those fields. The create() handler already normalises these to Number|null before POST, but runStockCheck() was not updated to do the same. Two possible fixes: (A) normalise on the client (preferred, one-liner) or (B) add a Pydantic pre-validator on RequestIn that converts '' → None for Optional[float] fields (also useful for future clients).
